The student converts the bearing to a 30° angle from south, uses cosine to find the distance along the path that gives 40 km south, then converts distance and speed to time in minutes. This is a multi-step bearing, trig and rate problem with no scaffolding.

content.prompt:
A fishing boat leaves a jetty and travels on a bearing of $150^\circ$ at a constant speed of $30\text{ km/h}$.
How long, to the nearest minute, will it take for the boat to be $40\text{ km}$ further south than the jetty?

answer.worked:
The bearing $150^\circ$ is $180^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ$ east of south. Let $d$ be the distance travelled in kilometres.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 30^\circ&=\frac{40}{d}\\d&=\frac{40}{\cos 30^\circ}\end{align*}$$
The time taken is
$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{40}{30\cos 30^\circ}\text{ hours}\\&=\frac{80}{\cos 30^\circ}\text{ minutes}\\&\approx92\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$
The journey takes 1 hour 32 minutes.
